sources.confirmDeleteCopies: Also delete the {{count}} copies it imported? Press Cancel to keep them as manual copies.

humble.description: Imports every key in your Humble Bundle orders: unrevealed, revealed, gifted and expired. Hidden keys are never revealed.
humble.sessionCookieHelp:
1. Open the page above and sign in to Humble Bundle.
2. Open DevTools (F12, or Cmd+Option+I on a Mac) → Application → Cookies → `https://www.humblebundle.com`.
3. Copy the value of `_simpleauth_sess` and paste it here.
The cookie expires after a while: paste a new one when scans start failing.

steam.description: Imports your Steam library with the official Steam Web API.
steam.apiKeyHelp: Free key from Steam: open the page above, sign in and register any domain name (for example `localhost`).
steam.profileHelp:
Your SteamID64, custom URL name or full profile URL.
"Game details" must be Public in your Steam privacy settings.

sources.syncingHint: Large accounts can take a few minutes; progress is written to the server log.

epic.description: Imports the games in your Epic Games Store library, including the free weekly games you claimed. It signs in like the Epic launcher does (the same way Heroic and Legendary work) and only reads your library.
epic.authCodeHelp:
1. Open the page above and sign in to Epic. If Epic emails you a sign-in code, it goes on Epic's page, not here.
2. Epic then shows a short text. Copy the value of `authorizationCode` (32 letters and digits), or the whole text, and paste it here.
3. Press Test connection or Save right away: codes work once and expire within minutes.
Only needed the first time, or if the session expires after a long time without scans.

gog.description: Imports the games in your GOG library. It signs in like the GOG Galaxy client does (the same way Heroic and Playnite work) and only reads your library.
gog.authCodeHelp:
1. Open the page above and sign in to GOG.
2. GOG then opens an almost blank page whose address starts with `embed.gog.com/on_login_success`.
3. Copy that whole address from the address bar and paste it here (or just the part after `code=`).
4. Press Test connection or Save right away: codes work once and expire quickly.
Only needed the first time, or if the session expires.

battlenet.description: Imports the games in your Battle.net account (Blizzard and Activision titles, including classic games like Diablo II). Battle.net has no public library API and its sign-in has a captcha, so it reuses your browser's session on account.battle.net, the way Playnite does. It only reads your account.
battlenet.cookiesHelp:
1. Open the page above and sign in to Battle.net.
2. Open DevTools (F12, or Cmd+Option+I on a Mac) → Network, and reload the page.
3. Click the first request (`overview`) → Headers → Request Headers → `Cookie`.
4. Right-click its value → Copy value, and paste it here.
Game Vault renews the session by itself: paste new cookies only if a scan says you are signed out.

eaapp.description: Imports the games you own in the EA app (bought on EA's store, redeemed keys included; EA Play subscription games are skipped). EA has no public library API and its sign-in has a captcha, so it reuses your browser's session on accounts.ea.com and reads the library the EA app uses. It only reads your account.
eaapp.cookiesHelp:
1. Sign in on ea.com in your browser.
2. Open the page above. It should show a short text with `access_token`; if it says `login_required`, you are not signed in.
3. Open DevTools (F12, or Cmd+Option+I on a Mac) → Network, and reload the page.
4. Click the `auth?client_id=…` request → Headers → Request Headers → `Cookie`.
5. Right-click its value → Copy value, and paste it here.
Never share that page or the cookies: they give access to your EA account.

ubisoft.description: Imports the PC games in your Ubisoft Connect library (console games linked to the account are skipped). Ubisoft has no public library API and its sign-in has a captcha, so it reuses the session of Ubisoft's website, the way Lutris does. It only reads your account.
ubisoft.loginDataHelp:
1. Open the page above in a private window and sign in to Ubisoft with "Remember me" ticked. A private window keeps this login apart from your normal browser session: Ubisoft replaces the remember-me ticket every time Game Vault uses it, which would sign that browser out.
2. On that page, open DevTools (F12, or Cmd+Option+I on a Mac) → Application → Local Storage → `https://connect.ubisoft.com`.
3. Click the `PRODrememberMe` entry and copy its whole value.
4. Paste it here, then close the private window without signing out (signing out would revoke the ticket).
Paste a value once: after Game Vault uses it, the copied value stops working and Game Vault keeps the new ticket by itself. Never share that value: it gives access to your Ubisoft account.

xbox.description: Imports the games your Microsoft account owns in the Microsoft Store / Xbox (purchases and redeemed codes, for console and PC). Game Pass games, trials and add-ons are skipped. It signs in like the Xbox app does (the way Playnite works) and only reads your account.
xbox.codeHelp:
1. Open the page above and sign in with your Microsoft account (the one you use on Xbox).
2. Microsoft then opens an almost blank page whose address starts with `login.live.com/oauth20_desktop.srf?code=`.
3. Copy that whole address from the address bar and paste it here (or just the part after `code=`).
4. Press Test connection or Save right away: codes work once and expire within minutes.
Only needed the first time, or if the session expires after a long time without scans. Never share that address: it gives access to your Microsoft account.

playstation.description: Imports the PS4 and PS5 games bought with your PlayStation Network account (PS Plus games are skipped). It signs in like the PlayStation app does (the way psn-api and PSNAWP work) and only reads your account.
playstation.npssoHelp:
1. Sign in on playstation.com in your browser.
2. Open the page above. It shows a short text like `{"npsso":"…"}`; if it shows an error, you are not signed in.
3. Copy the `npsso` value (64 letters and digits), or the whole text, and paste it here.
Game Vault keeps a session that renews itself and uses the token again if needed; it lasts about two months. Never share it: it gives access to your PlayStation account.

amazon.description: Imports the games in your Amazon Games library: the ones you bought and the ones you claimed with Prime Gaming. It signs in like the Amazon Games launcher does (the way Heroic and nile work) and only reads your library. Prime Gaming codes for other stores (GOG, Epic…) are not part of it: those games appear when you scan that store.
amazon.codeHelp:
1. Open the page above and sign in to Amazon.
2. You land on amazon.com: copy the whole address from the browser's address bar (it contains `openid.oa2.authorization_code=`) and paste it here.
3. Press Test connection or Save right away: the address works once and expires within minutes.
The link is new every time Game Vault starts: if it fails, reload this page and open it again.
Game Vault appears as an Amazon Games device in your Amazon account; removing it there signs Game Vault out.

fanatical.description: Imports the game keys you bought on Fanatical, with the store each key is for (Steam, Epic, GOG…), its redeem deadline and the key itself once you have revealed it on Fanatical. Read-only: keys are never revealed or redeemed. DLC, software, books, audio and vouchers are not imported.
fanatical.consent: I understand the risk and use this at my own responsibility
fanatical.consentHelp:
Fanatical has no official way for other apps to read your account, and its Terms and Conditions do not allow it: they forbid to "take data from our website for your or third party databases or data harvests without our consent". Game Vault reads your key list the way the Playnite Fanatical plugin does. Fanatical could consider this a breach of its terms and suspend or close your account.
Game Vault only reads, once per scan, and scans only when you ask unless you schedule it. The authors of Game Vault are not responsible for what Fanatical does with your account. If you are not comfortable with that, do not add this source.
fanatical.sessionHelp:
1. Open the page above and sign in to Fanatical.
2. Open DevTools (F12, or Cmd+Option+I on a Mac) → Application → Local Storage → `https://www.fanatical.com`.
3. Copy the value of `bsauth` (it starts with `{"authenticated":true`) and paste it here.
The session expires after a while: paste a new value when scans say you are signed out. Never share it: it gives access to your Fanatical account.

itch.description: Imports the games in your itch.io library: the ones you bought, claimed for free, got in a bundle or were given. It uses itch.io's official API with a personal API key and only reads. Tools, assets, soundtracks, comics and books are not imported.
itch.apiKeyHelp:
1. Open the page above and sign in to itch.io.
2. Press Generate new API key and copy it.
3. Paste it here.
The key gives access to your itch.io account: never share it. Revoke it on the same page to disconnect Game Vault.

sources.excludedHint: Scans skip these items. Import one again to bring it back on the next sync.

system.configHint: Everything that changes lives in the config directory. Back it up and you have backed up Game Vault.
system.backupsHint: Backups are written to config/backups. Automatic backups run daily and the newest 14 are kept (configurable). To restore, stop the server, replace config/gamevault.db with a backup and copy config/backups/photos into config/photos.
system.csvIntro: For physical games and stores without an API. Re-importing the same file updates rows instead of duplicating them.
system.importDone: {{added}} copies added, {{updated}} updated, {{unchanged}} unchanged, {{games}} new games.
system.csvColumns: Columns: title (required), platform, kind (key / library / physical), status, key, redeemBy, origin, acquiredOn, edition, grade (sealed, mint, very_good, good, acceptable, damaged), contents (box manual media extras), location, price (29.95), currency (EUR), notes, links (store:id pairs separated by spaces, e.g. steam:620), externalId, barcode. Comma or semicolon separated; dates as YYYY-MM-DD.
system.currencyHelp: Used for new prices and for CSV rows without a currency.
system.currencyNotSaved: Proposed from your browser region, not saved yet: save it so CSV rows without a currency use it.
system.photoStore: Photos in backups: {{size}} in all; each photo is stored once, however many backups have it.
system.valueShop: {{name}} sells your collection for {{sell}} and would pay {{cash}} in cash ({{credit}} in credit)
system.valueOther_one: {{count}} estimate in another currency is not included
system.valueOther_other: {{count}} estimates in other currencies are not included
system.valueNoCurrency: Choose a default currency in Preferences to add up the estimates.

logs.settingsIntro: Logs are written to config/logs. When the current file reaches the maximum size it is archived, and only the newest files are kept. Changes apply immediately.
logs.maxTotal: Logs will never use more than about {{mb}} MB.
logs.confirmClear: Delete every archived log file? The current file is kept.

providers.title: Metadata providers
providers.intro: Like Plex agents: for each kind of data, enabled providers are tried from top to bottom and the first one with an answer wins. The others act as fallbacks.
providers.coversIntro: Each provider only applies to the games it can cover, so keyed providers do not spend their quota on games another source covers better.

custom.name: Chosen or custom cover
custom.description: A cover you picked with "Choose cover" or pasted as a URL in the game page.

providers.confirmRedownload: Drop every cached cover? They are downloaded again as you browse, which spends provider quota.
providers.retried_one: {{count}} game will be looked up again.
providers.retried_other: {{count}} games will be looked up again.
providers.redownloaded_one: {{count}} cover dropped; it will be downloaded again.
providers.redownloaded_other: {{count}} covers dropped; they will be downloaded again.

thegamesdb.description: Platform-specific box art (the Xbox 360 case for an Xbox 360 disc). Used for games with a physical copy, games no store knows, and store games no store had art for. One request per game, then cached.
thegamesdb.apiKeyHelp:
Request a free key on TheGamesDB forums (page above).
Keys have a monthly request allowance; Test checks the key without spending it, and tells you when it is used up.

steam.description: Steam library art for games linked to Steam. No key and no quota.

providers.barcodesIntro: Used by Scan to identify a disc from the barcode on its box. Unknown codes are identified once by title and then remembered.

cex.description: The second-hand game store's catalog: free, no key, and it knows many European (PAL) editions that other databases miss. Each country has its own catalog; they are asked one by one, and the countries that found your games are asked first next time. Only the name and platform are used.
cex.countriesHelp: Leave empty to look up barcodes in every country. To limit it, list country codes separated by commas: uk, es, ie, pt, au, in, mx, it, pl. CeX prices use the same countries, in this order (Spain when empty).

upcitemdb.description: Free, no key needed (about 100 lookups a day). Knows most US boxes and about half of European ones.
upcitemdb.userKeyHelp: Only for a paid UPCitemdb plan with a higher limit. Leave empty to use the free endpoint.

eansearch.description: European product database with good PAL coverage (it knows Xbox 360 boxes that free databases miss). Needs an API token: trial 1 € the first month (100 lookups), Pro 19 €/month (5,000). Test checks the token and tells you when it has no credits left.
eansearch.tokenHelp:
1. Open the page above and create an EAN-Search.org account with API access.
2. Copy your API token and paste it here.
You can cancel any time, for example after cataloguing your collection.

local.name: Your catalog
local.description: Barcodes you already registered are recognised instantly, without asking any database.

ebay.description: Finds eBay listings with the scanned EAN. Best free option for old European (PAL) games, which second-hand sellers list with their barcode. Needs free eBay developer keys.
ebay.keysHelp:
1. Open the page above and create a free eBay developer account.
2. Go to Application Keys → Production keyset and copy the App ID and Cert ID.
3. If asked about marketplace account deletion notifications, choose the exemption: Game Vault does not store eBay user data.
ebay.marketplacesHelp: Tried in order until one has listings; the first one is also used for prices. Default: EBAY_ES, EBAY_GB, EBAY_DE, EBAY_FR, EBAY_IT.

providers.metadataIntro: Summary, genres, companies, trailers and screenshots shown in each game. The first provider gives the main sheet; the next ones fill what is missing. Downloaded when you open a game, then cached for 30 days.

steamDetails.description: Steam store page of games linked to Steam: summary in your language, genres, companies, Metacritic, trailers and screenshots. Free, no key.

thegamesdbDetails.description: Platform-specific overview (English), genres, companies, age rating, players and YouTube trailer, for games with a physical copy or not linked to any store. Uses the TheGamesDB key from Covers; about 2 requests per game, then cached.

epicCovers.description: Official box art from the Epic Games Store, for games imported from your Epic library. Free, no key needed.

gogCovers.description: Official box art from GOG, for games imported from your GOG library. Free, no key needed.

ubisoftCovers.description: Box art from Ubisoft Connect for games imported from your Ubisoft library, else the Ubisoft Store packshot (also for Ubisoft Connect keys). Free, no key needed.

eaCovers.description: Official pack art from EA, for games imported from your EA library. Free, no key needed.

battlenetCovers.description: Blizzard publishes no box art outside its signed-in shop, so games imported from Battle.net are looked up on the Steam store by their exact title (many Blizzard and Activision games are sold there too). Games only on Battle.net fall back to the other providers. Free, no key needed.

xboxCovers.description: Official poster from the Microsoft Store, for games imported from your Microsoft account. Free, no key needed.

cexPrices.description: What CeX sells your physical games for, and what it pays for them in cash or store credit. Only your own copies with a barcode are asked, one at a time.
cexPrices.countriesHelp: Shared with CeX barcode lookups. CeX stores to ask, in order, separated by commas: es, uk, ie, pt, it… The first that sells the product gives its price, in its currency. Empty: es.

ebayPrices.description: The median asking price of used listings with the copy's barcode on your first eBay marketplace. Uses the same developer keys as eBay barcode lookups.

providers.valuationsIntro: Second-hand prices of your physical copies with a barcode. Every enabled source is asked, each copy on its own date about once a month; the order is only how they are listed.

fields.title: Fields
fields.intro: Your own fields for games and copies: where you bought it, how long it took, a rating, a shelf… They appear in the game sheet, in this order, and you can search and filter by them.
fields.confirmDelete: Delete the field “{{name}}”? Its values in {{games}} and {{copies}} will be removed. This cannot be undone.
fields.empty: No fields yet. Add one to record anything the catalog does not track: a rating, a shelf, the price you paid…
fields.name: Name
fields.kindsHint: With none ticked, every kind of copy has the field.
fields.decimalsInUse: Fixed while games hold a value: clear them to change it.
fields.removeAppliesNow: Removing a saved value applies at once, without Save.
fields.mergeInto: Games and copies with this value get
fields.fixedAfterCreate: The type and whether it describes a game or a copy cannot change later.
fields.invalidNumber: Not a valid number: fix it or clear it to save.

coverPicker.title: Choose cover
coverPicker.intro: Images proposed by your enabled cover providers. The one you pick is kept even if the provider order changes.
coverPicker.none: No provider has a cover for this game. Link it to a store (Edit → Store links) or paste an image URL.

scan.title: Scan
scan.intro: Add physical games by their barcode: point the camera at box after box, use a USB or Bluetooth reader, or type the code. Each box joins the list below; Send adds them all at once.
scan.invalid: "{{code}}" is not a valid barcode (check the digits).

camera.hint: Point at the barcode on the back of the box
camera.insecure: The camera needs HTTPS (or localhost). On your phone, open Game Vault through an HTTPS address.
camera.denied: Camera permission denied. Allow it in the browser settings for this site.
camera.hintLaptop: Hold the barcode 20–30 cm from the camera, level and in good light

batch.label: Every box gets
batch.hint: Applied to every game you add from here; remembered on this device.

list.title: Scanned ({{count}})
list.empty: Scan a box to start: each one joins this list, and nothing is added until you press Send.
list.repeat: {{code}} is already in the list: use +1 on its row for another copy.
list.plusOneTitle: One more copy of this box
list.sendFailed: Nothing was sent: {{error}}. The list is unchanged.
list.noStorage: This browser does not let Game Vault keep the list: it will be lost if the page closes.
list.unknown: Not in any barcode database: write the title and search. The box keeps its barcode, so next time it is recognized at once.

login.title: Sign in
login.intro: Game Vault is protected. Sign in with your user.

setup.title: Create your user
setup.intro: Create the user to sign in from other devices. On trusted networks (by default, this computer) you can also get in without it.

notAllowed.title: Access not authorised
notAllowed.noUser: No user has been created yet. Open Game Vault from a trusted network (by default, the computer running it, at http://127.0.0.1:8080) and create one in System → Security.

security.title: Security

authentication.label: Authentication
authentication.trusted_networksHelp: Requests from the trusted networks below get in without signing in; everyone else signs in with the user and password.
authentication.requiredHelp: Everyone signs in with the user and password, this computer included. If you forget the password, start Game Vault with -reset-auth.

networks.label: Trusted networks
networks.help: One network (192.168.1.0/24) or address (192.168.1.20) per line. By default only this computer (in Docker, your local network). Requests through a proxy, or that use a host name instead of an address, are never trusted.

certificates.label: Certificate validation
certificates.help: Whether Game Vault checks the HTTPS certificates of the stores and services it connects to. Keep it enabled unless a proxy or a local service uses its own certificate.

user.title: User
user.createIntro: Create the user to sign in from other devices, or to make authentication required.
user.changeIntro: Changing the password signs out every other session. From a trusted network it can be reset without the current one.
user.changed: User saved; other sessions were signed out.

security.youAreTrusted: You are in without signing in: this request comes from a trusted network.

details.empty: No provider has details for this game yet.
details.emptyNoLinks: No details found. Link the game to a store (Edit → Store links) or enable TheGamesDB in Providers.

photos.title: Photos of the copy
photos.unreadable: This browser cannot read that image. Pick a JPEG or PNG (on an iPhone, set Camera → Formats → Most Compatible).
photos.tooMany_one: A copy can have at most {{max}} photos: {{count}} photo was not added.
photos.tooMany_other: A copy can have at most {{max}} photos: {{count}} photos were not added.
photos.caption: Caption
photos.confirmDelete: Delete this photo from the copy?

value.addBarcode: Add the barcode to estimate its price

connector.waiting: Sign in in the tab that opened…
connector.install: One click with the Game Vault Connector browser extension. Already installed? Open its icon on this page and press Enable.
connector.update: Update the Game Vault Connector extension to connect this store.
connector.privateOn: Opens in a private window, so this browser stays signed in to the store.
connector.privateOff: To keep this browser signed in, allow the extension in incognito (its details page in the browser's extensions). Otherwise it opens in a normal tab, and Game Vault's use of the session will sign this browser out of the store.

error.denied: The extension was not allowed to read that store, or this address is not enabled: open the extension's icon and press Enable on this address.
error.invalid: This store's sign-in recipe is not valid; update Game Vault.
error.unsupported: Update the Game Vault Connector extension.
error.timeout: The sign-in took too long; try again.
error.failed: The extension could not finish the sign-in; try again or paste the value by hand.
